parallel.requirements: The parallel-mode main agent recognized ESM .mjs output, manual argparse-compatible --a handling, no external npm modules, black-box executable probing, and matching <Schema: ['content']> output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although the session entered swarm mode, the main agent decided the task was small and tightly coupled, did not spawn subagents, and owned probing, implementation, verification, and final response itself.
parallel.implementation: It probed normal, missing, help, repeated, inline, prefix, separator, negative-looking, empty, and unknown argument cases; then wrote pyrepr.mjs, argparse.mjs, analysis.mjs, fields.mjs, and test3.mjs.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The main agent wrote all deliverable files directly under /output with local .mjs imports and artifact validation later listed test3.mjs plus four library files.
parallel.verification: It ran a 17-case comparison harness against the executable, noticed an exit-code capture bug caused by a pipeline, corrected the harness, and obtained OK results for all selected cases.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Despite self-verification, the official completed evaluator marked the solution failed with 150/171 samples; the mounted records do not expose per-case failures or a coordination cause.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM .mjs, local-module, zero-dependency, manual --a parsing, black-box probing, and Schema repr obligations from the prompt.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial control used a single main agent throughout, with no delegation, and directly owned executable probing, module implementation, local checks, and final response.
serial.implementation: It probed normal output, missing argument, missing value, extra positional, unknown flag, help, inline --a=value, and repeated --a; then wrote argparse.mjs, analysis.mjs, fields.mjs, and test3.mjs.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The main agent wrote the entry file and three libraries under /output with explicit .mjs local imports; artifact validation later listed test3.mjs and the three library files.
serial.verification: It ran selected local Node checks and reported byte-for-byte alignment except for program basename behavior that it considered argparse-faithful.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official completed evaluator also marked the serial solution failed with 150/171 samples, leaving the same aggregate residual shortfall without mounted per-test failure details.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were likewise no child briefs or handoffs in serial; the main agent kept all task context locally.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel-mode main compared 17 selected argument cases, first found a harness exit-code bug, fixed it, and reported all selected cases OK.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both solutions failed with the same 150/171 score. The concrete process difference is that the nominal parallel run entered swarm mode but never executed child agents, then did broader direct probing and wrote one extra helper module; the serial control did a smaller direct implementation. The mounted evidence therefore supports a process-style difference, not a discordant result or a parallel coordination failure.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel added lib/pyrepr.mjs and probed more argparse edge cases, including negative-looking values, separator cases, prefix help, and empty values.
Serial embedded the list repr helper in fields.mjs and performed fewer local checks.
Both self-selected verification sets missed some official evaluator cases, but the mounted records expose only aggregate failures.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference and no retained parallel coordination pattern

candidates.reason: The main agent owned and performed implementation directly; no executed child-agent split left implementation ownerless.
No multiple component agents existed, and the main wrote the entry and libraries itself, so no cross-agent integration owner was missing.
The main agent wrote the final /output/test3.mjs deliverable and artifact validation found it, so final assembly was not unowned.
The run had one main actor owning exploration, implementation, local verification, and final response; no delegated pipeline transition was unowned.
Executable probing was the main agent's own pre-implementation research; no child workers or productive parallel capacity were blocked behind a gate.
The investigation was not performed by overlapping investigators and did not defer delegated implementation; the main simply probed then implemented.
There were no available child workers assigned to auxiliary work and no starved child-owned critical path; the main did all work directly.
The protocol recorded zero delegation and zero subagents, so there was no fan-out breadth or retry swarm that could exhaust budget.
No child task was issued at all, so no single child received an overbroad assignment or left child-owned work unfinished.
No child brief was sent; all known task requirements remained in the main agent context, so a brief omission cannot be evidenced.
No separately owned components were delegated to different agents, so there was no absent cross-agent file, export, or compatibility contract.
There was no inter-actor transfer where a known finding or constraint disappeared; the same main agent consumed its own probes.
No child returned a large handoff to the parent, and no available result was left unconsumed due to excessive report volume.
No receiver consumed a superseded child handoff; all observed state updates and verification were local to the main agent.
No incompatible reports or child contracts reached a parent decision point, because no child reports were produced.
The main performed local whole-script checks before final response; the official failure alone is hidden evaluator evidence and cannot establish this label.
The provider retry record shows one attempt and no replacement child or retry lacking inherited checkpoints.

The run did not time out or wait on children; the main continued through probes, writes, checks, and completion.
Only the main agent wrote implementation files; no concurrent agents produced competing cross-file designs.
There were no live concurrent file editors, so no same-file collision or reconciliation of another agent's change occurred.
